stages.name: Investigate
stages.instructions: Investigate the task and relevant project files. Explain the root cause or requirements, cite evidence, and propose a concrete implementation plan. Do not change project code.

stages.name: Implement
stages.instructions: Implement the task using the prior findings. Follow project conventions, run appropriate checks, and report what changed and any remaining issues.

stages.name: Review (optional)
stages.instructions: Review the implementation and test evidence. Do not modify code. Distinguish blocking correctness issues and failed required checks from advisory suggestions. Give an explicit pass or needs_changes verdict.

stages.name: Review summary
stages.instructions: Write a review brief for the person who will review this work. Use the original task, the prior stage handoffs and artifacts, and the actual changes in the working directory; inspect them with read-only commands such as git status, git diff --stat, and git diff, and never run commands that change files or Git state. Put the whole brief in the handoff summary as Markdown with these sections: ## Outcome (whether the task was done, partly done, or not, in one or two sentences); ## Changes (each changed file or area: what changed and why); ## Verification (checks actually run and their results as reported by prior stages or the router, and plainly what was not verified); ## Review focus (the specific places to read closely: risky logic, behavior changes, assumptions, deviations from the plan, with file references); ## Open questions (decisions for the reviewer, known limitations, follow-ups); ## Try it (commands or steps to exercise the change, if any). Be concrete and brief and cite files. List changed files in files_changed. Leave findings, tests, and unresolved empty because earlier stages already report them. If the sandbox stops you writing the handoff file, finish with the handoff block in your final message and do not mention it in the brief. Do not modify project files, commit, push, or publish.
